evals.prompt: My W&B sweep agent loop calls train(), which does `run = wandb.init(project='p', config=cfg)` and never calls finish(). When a trial throws, my agent loop catches the exception and moves to the next trial. What state do those failed trials end up in on W&B, and do I need `with wandb.init(...)`?
expectations: Says a run whose exception is caught by the caller is recorded as finished (exit code 0), not failed
Says an uncaught crash is still marked failed even without the context manager (wandb hooks sys.excepthook)
Recommends `with wandb.init(...) as run:` or run.finish(exit_code=1) in the except path
Does not claim the run stays 'running' forever
evals.verified_facts: Executed offline on wandb 0.28.2 and 0.31.0, state read with `wandb leet inspect`: no `with` + uncaught raise -> failed (exit 1); no `with` + exception caught by caller -> finished (exit 0); `with` + caught -> failed (exit 1).

evals.prompt: I log my training config to W&B through this skill's obslog package (copy it from the skill's assets) using redact_config, as in evals/files/redact_config/train.py. Which keys of CONFIG end up in W&B readable, and which get redacted? I need max_tokens, tokenizer, num_passes and author visible in the W&B UI.
expectations: Reports which keys the obslog redact_config redacts based on actually reading or running the code (not guessing)
The setup the answer leaves the user with (as shipped, or after a fix the answer provides) sends lr, max_tokens, tokenizer, num_passes and author to W&B unredacted
hf_token is redacted (or kept out of the config) in the setup the answer leaves the user with
evals.verified_facts: Executed: the original skill's redact_config (substring match on secret-like words) redacts max_tokens, tokenizer, num_passes and author as well as hf_token. The revised word-based matcher redacts only hf_token. An answer using the original asset passes assertion 2 only if it notices the over-redaction and gives a working fix.

evals.prompt: In evals/files/thread_context/service.py (Python 3.13, default build), do the 'resizing' log records carry the request_id bound with this skill's ContextVar filter? Explain why, and fix it minimally.
expectations: Answers no: records logged inside the ThreadPoolExecutor worker do not carry the request_id
Explains that pool.submit runs the function in the worker thread's own context, not a copy of the caller's context
Fix uses contextvars.copy_context().run (or asyncio.to_thread, which copies context, or re-binding inside the worker)
Does not claim ContextVars automatically follow work into thread pools
evals.verified_facts: Executed on 3.11-3.14 default builds: pool.submit(fn) -> request_id None; pool.submit(copy_context().run, fn) -> id present; asyncio.to_thread -> present; run_in_executor -> absent. Only free-threaded 3.14t or -X thread_inherit_context=1 inherit context in new threads.

evals.prompt: I'm on wandb 0.31.0, I ran `wandb login`, and I start runs with this skill's obslog start_run(). (a) Will my runs go online? (b) If the W&B server is unreachable for an hour, does my training job die?
expectations: (a) Correctly states whether runs go online after `wandb login` on wandb 0.31 given the start_run/resolve_mode code it read (see facts), and if that code would silently go offline, says so and gives a fix

(b) Correctly states whether the job dies when the server is unreachable given the code it read, and leaves the user with a setup that does not die (fallback to offline after CommError, either already present or added by the answer)
Mentions `wandb sync` to upload offline runs later
Does not recommend relying on grepping ~/.netrc for api.wandb.ai as the credential check on 0.31
evals.verified_facts: Two versions of the skill's obslog/wandb_run.py exist and the answer may have read either. Version 1: resolve_mode greps ~/.netrc for 'api.wandb.ai'; wandb 0.31.0's default host is api.forge.coreweave.com and `wandb login` writes `machine api.forge.coreweave.com`, so version 1 returns offline (runs silently go offline); version 1's start_run has no CommError handling, so with the server unreachable wandb.init raises CommError after about 90 s and the job dies before training. Version 2: resolve_mode calls wandb.login(prompt=False, verify=False), so runs go online; start_run catches CommError and retries offline. Judge (a) and (b) against the version the answer describes. An answer about version 1 passes (a) and (b) only if it identifies the problem and gives a working fix. Once a run is up, a later outage does not kill training (logging is buffered by the local service).

evals.prompt: Write resume logic for a preemptible PyTorch training job that may run with WANDB_MODE=offline. It should keep a stable W&B run id across restarts and resume from the last checkpoint.
expectations: Decides whether to resume by checking that the checkpoint file exists, not by checking run.resumed
Does not call wandb.util.generate_id()
Persists the run id to a file next to the checkpoint and reuses it on restart
Notes that in offline mode run.resumed is False (and run.step starts at 0) even when resuming
evals.verified_facts: Executed on 0.28.2 and 0.31.0 offline: resume='allow'/'must' keeps the same id but run.resumed is False and step 0. wandb.util.generate_id does not exist (AttributeError).

evals.prompt: My JSON log lines from a single-process app have the traceback stuffed inside the `message` field instead of a structured `exc_info` field. I'm using a stock logging.handlers.QueueHandler in front of my JSON handler. Why, and how do I fix it?
expectations: Says QueueHandler.prepare() formats the message (merging the traceback into msg) and clears exc_info/exc_text
Fix overrides prepare() to return the record unmodified (or otherwise preserves exc_info) for the single-process case
Notes the stock behavior exists for multiprocessing/pickling safety
evals.verified_facts: CPython logging/handlers.py QueueHandler.prepare calls self.format(record), sets record.msg to the formatted message and record.exc_info/exc_text to None. Unchanged area in both versions.
